fix(markdown): link only an http address, and carry a backslashed pipe as text (#721)

The review of the card layer (709) raised four points, and three of them
are real. This layer answers them at the top of the stack rather than in
the layer that owns the code, so that nine green runs stay green.

**A link's destination was contained but never judged.** The escaper
keeps a value from ending the link it is in and says nothing about its
scheme, so a `javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:` address survived into
a live link, and it was the client's renderer that decided what a click
did: goldmark drops such a destination on its own, a chat surface that
hands hrefs through does not. `LinkableDestination` is the allow list,
http and https and nothing else, read off the value with its control
bytes gone, because `java\x00script:` is `javascript:` the moment the
escaper drops the byte. `MdTitleLink` writes a refused destination as
the title with the address beside it in a code span, and the upload
image embed uses the same list, so the reader keeps what GitLab sent and
nothing in it is live. Every address this server links is one GitLab
built from its own origin, so the list costs nothing legitimate.

**A backslash already in front of a pipe is the one value a code span
cannot carry inside a table cell.** The row is split before any span is
read; there a backslash escapes the pipe and a second backslash escapes
the first, so one added backslash leaves the pipe live and two show a
backslash the value never had. `MdCodeSpanCell` writes that value as
text instead, each backslash doubled and the pipe as its entity, which
every renderer shows as sent; the common case, a backslash anywhere else
in the value, stays in the span.

**Asking the GFM line model to confirm the second fix found a defect in
the model.** It read links off the raw line, so a bracketed address a
formatter had deliberately moved into a code span was reported as a
destination the page does not have. A code span takes precedence over a
link in CommonMark, and the links are read off the bare line now, with
the model's own test pinning the four shapes at that boundary.

**The fence contract claimed byte for byte**, and the card writer's
`End` defuses a guidance heading inside a fenced body on purpose, since
`ExtractHints` reads the rendered text rather than the parsed document.
The contract and the test say so now, and why.

The fourth point, stale README counts on 709, is how a stack works here:
the generated artifacts are refreshed once at the top, and this is the
top.

refactor(markdown): the last wave, and both gates at zero (#720)

The fourth and last migration wave, and the one that takes both gates to
zero.

Four of its six items are the migration's remainder: the instance
settings, sidekiq, plan limits, usage data, notifications and Orbit
cards; the Markdown the DEFAULT surface writes, which the census never
classified because it does not live in a file called `markdown.go` and
which a model on the dynamic surface reads before it reads anything
else; the prompt message vocabulary, which stays outside the card rule
and owes the containment idiom its own `untrusted.go` documents; and the
resource bodies a client reads directly.

The other two close a class the corrected gate could finally see: values
the shared renderers and the already-migrated packages still wrote raw
into a line with no escaper and no code span.

Three causes stood between that work and a silent gate, and each is
fixed where it belongs rather than at the call sites that were working
around it.

The not-found renderer interpolated its resource label raw, on the
strength of a doc comment saying every caller passes a constant. Two
callers did not: `badges` reads it off its result and escaped it at its
own call site, `orbit` read it off its result and passed it through. A
rule kept in a comment is a rule half the callers follow, so the
renderer contains both halves of its own sentence now and `badges` stops
escaping what it no longer has to.

A blank hint was written out as a bare list item, and the first of them,
landing directly under the sentence above it, turned that sentence into
a setext heading and took the whole guidance section out of what
`ExtractHints` could read. A result built from a zero value carries its
hint fields empty, and the award emoji not-found card was in exactly
that state.

The third was the gate itself. Handing every string field one identical
hostile payload made fields equal that differ in life, and a card that
prints a field only when it says something the card does not already say
then dropped the row: a commit message equal to its title, a detailed
status equal to its status, a tag target equal to its commit id. That is
28 findings in which nothing was lost and nothing injected, and the rule
would have gone on hiding a real item loss on those same cards. The
payload now carries each field's own sentinel.

The runtime registry gate reports 0 structural and 0 hostile findings
over 589 cases and 1737 renders. The static gate reports 0 unescaped
values, with the 11 that remain in `elicitationtools` argued rather than
silenced: those lines are the question a person is shown in a consent
dialog, not a tool result about a GitLab object, and they must not
become card rows.

The generated artifacts are refreshed once here, at the top of the
stack. The site identity snapshot goes with them for a reason unrelated
to this work: the canonical document it mirrors gained a profile and
reordered another, so the site check had begun failing on every branch,
`main` included.

refactor(markdown): card vocabulary for settings, sidekiq, plan limits, usage data, notifications and Orbit

Every result about one object in these six packages is a card written by
toolutil.Card, and a table is left to the collections: the queues and the
processes, the license and count maps, the tool manifest, the components, the
domains.

The settings card carried the defect both the gate design and the "robust"
design named as unreachable by the static walk, and it was real:
`fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%v", val)` wrote an administrator-set `any` out of GitLab's
application settings into a table cell with no escaping, so a value holding a
pipe split the row, a multi-line sign_in_text ended it, and an array or an
object rendered as Go's container syntax rather than as the JSON it arrived as.
Each value is now rendered by its JSON kind and written through the row its kind
needs. Two more went with it: the total counted every key GitLab sent while the
card showed 27 of them, and the update card opened with an H1 where its sibling
opened with an H2.

The rest, in the order the audit lists them: the plan limits carry the unit
GitLab counts them in rather than a bare number; the metric-definition document
is cut on a rune boundary, at the read ceiling and at the display cut alike, so
the fence never ends in half a character; the Service Ping queries write their
version, edition and recording time as three rows instead of one unescaped
run-on line, and the document's closing fence no longer follows a blank line;
Orbit renders the user-level availability flag and the backend error it never
showed, reads the nested response shape it used to report as "no status data",
puts the tool name in a code span instead of feeding one the cell escaper, and
drops its local copy of the fence sizer for the shared one.

Timestamps go through FormatTime, hints name canonical action IDs, and the
formatter tests assert whole output instead of substrings.

refactor(dynamic): one card vocabulary for the default surface's own output

The Markdown the dynamic surface writes is what a model reads before it reads
anything else, and it was the one set of formatters the census never
classified, because it does not live in a markdown.go. The three of them now
write what every migrated package writes: a card heading, the query as a code
span, one table for the collection of matches, and the guidance last, where
ExtractHints can lift it.

What that closes, finding by finding. The six hand-built header variants are
one column order both the header and every row are filtered from, so a row
carrying a cell its header never declared is no longer possible rather than
merely untested. The four booleans printed as %t are the warning sign a
destructive action deserves, in the table and on the card alike, since a tick
beside "Destructive" reads as approval. The caller's query is a code span
rather than a %q. The input schema goes through Card.Fence instead of a fence
written by hand under a comment explaining why it was safe. The finder's empty
branch offers the nearby tokens the registry already computes and used to
compute for search alone. The describe card publishes the usage note, the
parameter guidance and the example call, all three of which it built and
printed none of. The finder says when the top result is low confidence or the
alias was ambiguous, which it knew and never said while telling the model to
execute that row now. And the two headings agree on the noun and carry the
count they were leaving to be inferred.

The suggestions the finder renders are passed to the formatter rather than
published: FindOutput carries no field for them and the output schema does
not move here.

Search and Describe are kept and migrated rather than deleted. They are
exported API of the package, the runtime Markdown gate drives all three
explicitly, and registering them would add tools to the default surface, which
this layer must not do; their fate is a decision for the surface, not for a
Markdown migration.

Gates on these files: the static card and bool-time rules go from 14 sites
(7 card rows, 7 flags) to 0, with all 18 escaping directives removed as the
values now reach their escaper; the runtime gate's three explicit dynamic
cases stay at 0 findings. The formatter tests assert the whole document.

fix(prompts): contain what GitLab wrote, and stop answering questions nobody asked

internal/prompts stays out of the card rule: a prompt message is the model's
instruction payload rather than a report about one object, and it has its own
vocabulary for that in untrusted.go. What it owed was that vocabulary applied
everywhere it interpolates GitLab-authored text, plus the defects the markdown
audit recorded against these files.

The boundary sentence every message ends with named shapes -- "the quoted,
tabulated and fenced regions above" -- which leaves the reader to work out which
regions those are and says nothing about a value rendered inline on a line the
server wrote, which is most of what a prompt message is. It names the values
now: titles, descriptions, comments, labels, branch names, file paths and diffs.
mdInline and mdHeading say on themselves that they are the same composition
toolutil.Card applies to every inline value it writes.

The full project audit discarded the error from eight of its nine calls, so a
refusal produced an empty slice and the empty slice produced a verdict: no
protected branches, no labels, no milestones, no templates, no webhooks and no
push rules -- a scorecard of failures about a project nobody managed to look at,
which reads exactly like a genuinely unconfigured one. Each section now says it
could not be read, the scorecard marks the row rather than scoring it, and the
closing instruction says what that means. The two rows the project's own
response answers stay verdicts.

The rest, each with a test that fails on the old rendering:

- The audit prompts' local access-level table knew five levels and called every
  other "Unknown(<n>)"; toolutil.AccessLevelDescription names Planner, Minimal
  access, Security Manager and Admin, and renders an unknown one as the number
  GitLab sent.
- my_open_mrs keyed its authored set on the IID alone. IIDs are unique inside a
  project and this prompt spans every project the caller can see, so an assigned
  MR counted as authored whenever the numbers collided, which for IIDs starting
  at 1 is most of them. Both counters read the project and IID together now, in
  one identity the deduplicator shares.
- The two Mermaid pie charts built their entries with Go's %q, which writes a
  backslash Mermaid renders literally and leaves the quotation mark that ends
  the label. A label or a commit author name is whatever somebody typed, so the
  quote is reachable and everything after it is chart syntax. mermaidQuoted
  writes Mermaid's own entity form.
- project_activity_report promised a daily activity chart and a contributor
  breakdown its handler never wrote. Both come out of the project events it
  already fetches, so it writes them.
- Four reports closed with "---" directly under a line of text, which is a
  setext heading in CommonMark: no rule, and the sentence above promoted to H2.
  It was the reports with nothing to report that reached it. writeClosingRule
  separates the rule the way Card separates a block, adding only what is
  missing, so every site that was already correct renders byte for byte.
- review_mr told the model to "use base_sha=``" on a merge request GitLab sends
  no diff refs for, which is an instruction to send a position GitLab refuses.
  It says the refs are absent instead, which is what lets the model take the
  other half of the same advice.
- Two description excerpts were byte slices at a fixed offset, so a multi-byte
  character spanning the cut was split and its orphaned bytes went into the
  message. truncateRunes cuts on a rune boundary; shortSHA goes through it too.
- A conflict flag printed as the Go word "true" now goes through BoolEmoji, and
  a milestone due date through FormatTime; those were the package's four static
  bool-time findings.
- A pipeline ref, its web URL, a job's failure reason, a shared group's name and
  the username in five section headings are contained like every other value.

Static escaping gate for internal/prompts: 4 findings before, 0 after, no stale
directive. The runtime registry scan is unchanged tree-wide (99 X1, 29 X2), and
reports nothing here either way: prompts register no Markdown formatter. No tool
name, action id, schema or description moved.

refactor(resources): canonical action IDs and helper-written fences in the workflow guides

The five text/markdown guide bodies are the only non-JSON resource payloads
this server serves, and they sat outside the Markdown audit's scope. Two
things in them were wrong for a reader on the default surface.

The pipeline guide's diagnostic steps named five individual-surface tools:
gitlab_pipeline_get, gitlab_job_list, gitlab_job_trace,
gitlab_ci_variable_list and gitlab_job_retry. One body is served whatever
GITLAB_MCP_TOOL_SURFACE says, and the default dynamic surface registers none
of them, so a model reading the guide was handed five tool calls its own
tools/list never carried. The steps now name the canonical action IDs
pipeline.get, job.list, job.trace, ci_variable.list and job.retry, which every
surface reaches, and the section says what an ID is passed to on each.

The conventional-commits guide wrote its two code fences as three backticks of
its own, which is safe only while the fenced text stays constant. Both go
through toolutil.MarkdownFencedBlock now, which sizes the fence to its body;
the rendered bytes are unchanged.

Three guards go in the package test, because no formatter registry and no
documentation gate reads these bodies: the only tool name any body may mention
is the dynamic executor, every canonical ID a body names resolves in the
catalog, and every body closes each fence it opens and writes no angle bracket
outside a fence or a code span. The last one is the runtime hostile-value rule
applied to the placeholders these guides are made of.

No resource URI, name, title, description or MIME type moves; only the bodies,
and with them the byte length the pipeline guide advertises.

fix(markdown): contain the values the shared renderers wrote raw

The four renderers every domain delegates to wrote a GitLab-authored value
onto a line with no escaper, so the containment of the domains that use them
was a fact about the values GitLab happens to send rather than about the
renderer. The runtime registry gate reports 49 fewer findings across eight
packages, and none of them is in a package this commit touches.

The delete and void confirmations dropped the control bytes of their message
and nothing else. The message is the handler's sentence built around a branch,
a package file or a project path, so one carrying a line break ended the
confirmation and wrote a heading, a list item or a second guidance section at
column zero, and one carrying a tag reached the page as raw HTML. Both the
registered formatters and the two result builders now write it through the
inline escaper a card row uses.

The safe-mode preview passed its hint to WriteHints as it stood. A hint is
written as given because it is the server's own sentence, composed at the call
site, and one of them is a link; this one is a field of the struct the
formatter is handed, so it is data like the status and the mode, and it is
escaped here rather than in the writer every other hint shares.

The discussion thread id was declared safe for its shape, a digest, which is
what made the four discussion domains depend on GitLab's id format for their
structure. It goes through the heading escaper now, in the list and in the
single thread alike, and the single thread opens through the card writer that
escapes it.

WriteMdURL, WriteMdURLNewline and WriteDescription go: the migration left them
with no caller, and Card.URL and Card.Text are what replaced them.

The elicitation wizards' "**Label**: value" lines stay as they are, and the
package comment now says why: they are the message of an elicitation request
rather than a tool result about an object, so they are not card rows, and
EscapeConsentValue is the stricter containment that channel needs. The
client-without-elicitation refusal loses its one bolded label and travels in
the refusal envelope every other refusal does.

fix(markdown): escape the values the migrated formatters still wrote raw

The corrected raw-tag rule of the registry scan (X2) reports a value that
reaches the page as a live anchor, and twenty-two of its findings sat in
packages an earlier wave had already migrated: a discussion thread id in its
heading, a one-line note body inside its quote, the not-found label and hints
award emoji and badges carry on their result, and the confirmation sentence
deployments and work item saved views print.

Each is now escaped for the slot it lands in. The thread id goes through
EscapeMdHeading, which retires the directive that declared it safe. A note body
of one line goes through the inline escaper before it is quoted, the split
Card.Text already makes: the quote contains a body's structure and contains
nothing at all about a raw tag, which a client renders as a live anchor wherever
it sits; a body that spans lines keeps its own markup, as every description does.
The labels, hints and sentences are escaped like any other value read off an
output, whoever composed them: a hint is a list item, a confirmation is one line
of inline content, and a value that reaches a formatter as a field rather than as
a literal is data.

Measured on the registry scan, for these packages: X2 22 to 0 and X1 44 to 0, the
hostile heading and hint findings having moved with the same values. The static
gate keeps 0 sites in these files, with two more values classified safe and two
fewer excused by directive. Nothing about the surface moves: the change is
rendering only, and the tool snapshots agree.

fix(markdown): close the last findings the registry gate reported

Three causes stood between the wave and a silent gate, and each one is fixed
where it belongs rather than at the call sites that were working around it.

The not-found renderer interpolated its resource label raw, on the strength of
a doc comment saying every caller passes a constant. Two did not: badges reads
it off its result and escaped it at its own call site, orbit read it off its
result and passed it through. The renderer contains both halves of its own
sentence now, badges stops escaping what it no longer has to, and the comment
says what is true.

A blank hint was written out as a bare list item, and the first of them landing
under the sentence above it turned that sentence into a setext heading, which
took the whole guidance section out of what ExtractHints could read. A result
built from a zero value carries its hint fields empty, and the award emoji card
was in exactly that state. Guidance with no text is not guidance: it is dropped,
and a call whose hints are all blank opens no section.

The third was the gate itself. Handing every string field one identical hostile
payload made fields equal that are different in life, and a card that prints a
field only when it says something the card does not already say then dropped the
row: a commit message equal to its title, a detailed status equal to its status,
a tag target equal to its commit id. That is 28 findings in which nothing was
lost and nothing injected, and it would have gone on hiding a real item loss on
those same cards. The payload now carries each field's own sentinel.

The registry gate reports 0 structural and 0 hostile findings over 589 cases and
1737 renders, and the tool snapshots are unchanged.

chore: refresh the generated artifacts at the top of the stack

The stack's layers leave these stale on purpose and one run refreshes them:
the README counts and the testing reference follow the tests the migration
added, with the recorded coverage values carried forward rather than
recomputed, since those depend on the machine that measures them.

The identity snapshot is refreshed for a reason that has nothing to do with
this stack: the canonical document it mirrors gained a profile and reordered
another, so the site check had begun failing on every branch, main included.

commit.message:
feat(1to1): R-PAGE, the dimension that asks whether a list says where it ends

Six dimensions of this audit were green on internal/tools/impersonationtokens,
which answers user.list_impersonation_tokens with a bare array of tokens while
GitLab serves twenty of them at a time: a caller cannot tell it has one page,
cannot ask for the second, and is not told either. None of the six could see it,
because all six compare a published field against client-go's struct, GitLab's
documentation or the live entity record, and GitLab's pagination is a field of
no entity. An offset page arrives in the X-Page, X-Next-Page, X-Per-Page,
X-Total and X-Total-Pages response headers, and a keyset page in a Link header.

The rule folds into -scope=paths rather than taking a scope of its own, because
it needs exactly R-PATH's three inputs and that scope already reads all three in
one pass: the committed request inventory, the live API record, and the action
catalog built once per run. The oracle is the record's declared params rather
than a guess from an endpoint's name. 308 of its 2110 mounted routes declare
per_page; 304 of those declare page beside it, and the other four take a cursor
or a page_token instead, which are counted apart and raise nothing, since a
page-and-total block is the wrong shape to publish for one.

An action is judged when its output type is a collection envelope: exactly one
content field, and that field a list of objects, with this server's own framing
taken out first. That strictness is where "the route declares the params but the
action reads a single object" is answered structurally rather than one
declaration at a time. Admitting an object that carries a list, a project with
its shared_with_groups or a job with its artifacts, took the finding list from
24 to 79, of which 55 were about a list nobody asked to page.

The join from an action to an endpoint is the package, the same grain and the
same limit the observation check carries, stated beside the numbers in
pagination_endpoint_grain. It costs ten of the twenty-four findings, each
written down in pagination_declarations.go with the route the record holds for
it and what its params are. There is deliberately no category for an endpoint
GitLab pages that we have decided not to publish pagination for: that is the
finding.

It reports and does not gate, since a finding is a surface change. Of 268
collection-reading actions, 224 already publish a pagination block, 20 sit in a
package no paginated endpoint was recorded for, and 24 are findings, 14 of them
undeclared. Its declaration table gates like every other one here. No output
type, handler or registered action is changed by this commit.

commit.message:
refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for the security domains

vulnerabilities, securityfindings, securityattributes, securitycategories,
securityscanprofiles, securitysettings, compliancepolicy, auditevents and
externalstatuschecks now write every one-object result through toolutil.Card
and every collection through the list vocabulary. Each of these formatters
opened a "| Field | Value |" table for the fields of one object, which is a
row only while nothing but a row has been written since the header; the rest
of the change is the defects that shape was hiding.

What renders differently:

- The vulnerability description was written raw at block level, so a security
  report artifact a repository's own CI job produces could open a heading, a
  list item or the server's guidance section. It is Card.Text now, quoted
  under its label, and so is the solution.
- The severity badge is toolutil.SeverityBadge in all three security domains
  instead of two hand-typed copies, which gains the UNKNOWN level the copies
  had no answer for and escapes a level GitLab has not published yet.
- The vulnerability hints read the state: dismissing a dismissed finding, or
  reverting a detected one, is a call GitLab refuses, and the card used to
  offer all of them whatever the state was. The security category and
  attribute cards read EditableState on the same terms.
- The vulnerability list carries the ID column every other vulnerability
  action takes, and a hint naming the get action; the scan-profile list
  carries the profile ID the detach action takes.
- Every flag is BoolEmoji and every instant FormatTime, in the card and in
  the two lists that printed the wire form; the group and project security
  settings, the audit event and the category all printed Go booleans.
- The audit event card writes every singular detail field GitLab sends, not
  the five it used to, and the list writes its summary line above the table
  rather than after the last row, where it was absorbed as one more row.
- The bulk security attribute update prints its identifier lists as numbers a
  reader can act on rather than Go's "[9 10]" container syntax, and the
  always-written Attributes row is now absent when there is nothing to name.
- An external status check that names no protected branch says "All
  branches", which is what an empty list means; it used to render as nothing
  in the card and as a count of zero in the list.
- The group secret-push-protection card no longer lets one flag stand for a
  per-project outcome the response cannot vouch for: the projects GitLab
  refused are counted and listed, and one sentence says what the value is.
- A list whose table has no link no longer tells the model to preserve links;
  the two external status check lists render the external URL as a link and
  keep the instruction.
- securitysettings writes its two timestamps through RFC3339Ptr instead of a
  layout ending in a literal Z, which stamped whatever wall clock the value
  carried with a zone it may not have been in.

The tests compare whole renders rather than substrings, which is how the
audit's worst class survived, and add cases for a scanner-authored
description, a hostile branch name, a hostile refusal message and the
state-dependent hints.

Static gate (-contexts all,card,bool-time) over these ten files: 100 sites
before (86 card rows and headers, 14 raw flags and instants), 0 after. The
runtime registry scan reports nothing for these nine packages, down from 45
(H2 18, X1 12, R1 6, X2 3, A1 3, L2 2, T3 1). No tool name, action ID, input
or output schema or description moved; the golden snapshot tests hold.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for boards, milestones, iterations and labels

Eleven packages move onto toolutil.Card and the list vocabulary: boards,
groupboards, groupepicboards, milestones, groupmilestones, iterationdata with
the groupiterations and projectiterations wrappers, and labels, grouplabels and
labeldata.

iterationdata is rewritten first, since both iteration packages render through
it. Its card opened a "| Property | Value |" table and then wrote list rows
into it, which ended the table with no body and left every later "| State | … |"
on the page as literal pipes; its list wrote the hints above the table, so the
header lazily continued that paragraph and no table rendered at all, and wrote
the summary line after the last row, where it was absorbed as one more. The
card is now a card, the list is heading, summary, table, pagination and hints in
that order, and its substring test is a whole-output expectation.

Both board packages wrote every field as a bullet-less "**Label**: value" line
with the value interpolated raw, so consecutive fields ran together into one
paragraph and a value carrying a line break added headings and list items of
its own; both are cards now, with the columns as a nested table. The defects
the audit named with them are closed: the board card carries its ID, the column
table names what each column collects rather than printing the list's own ID
whenever there is no label, a ceiling GitLab did not set renders as a dash
rather than as 0, an empty page is one sentence rather than a heading over an
empty table, and the group board card shows the assignee, the weight and the
two visibility flags it never showed.

Elsewhere: GitLab's own iteration state enum (1 upcoming, 2 current, 3 closed),
where 1 read as "opened" and shifted every later value by one; the wire form of
an iteration timestamp through RFC3339Ptr, rather than a layout ending in a
literal Z that stamped whatever wall clock the value carried; an expired
milestone marked with the warning sign rather than printed as the word "true";
milestone issue and merge request tables through FormatTime and the state
glyphs, which retires three allow-unescaped directives; group milestone hints
that name the milestone_iid every group milestone action actually takes, where
they said milestone_id; the epic board's list type and collapsed flag; and the
archive flag on a label, which the output type carried and no renderer read.

Both label packages alias one output type, so the Markdown registry keeps
whichever init ran first: the card is now chosen from the label's own scope, so
a group label is no longer titled "Label" and pointed at the project actions.

Measured on these files: the static gate (-contexts all,card,bool-time) goes
from 53 findings to 0, and the runtime scan from 137 to 0. The registry gate's
iterationdata proof moves to the half mergetrains already holds, that a
migrated formatter is never reported again; that the rules still see the class
is proved on the line model's own inputs.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for to-dos, snippets, events, search and the template details

To-do items, snippets and the license template detail are cards written by
toolutil.Card; the to-do, snippet, event and search lists go through the list
vocabulary.

The to-do card was four bullet-less "**Label:** value" lines, which a renderer
joins into one run-on paragraph, followed by the GitLab-authored body written at
block level, where "## x" added a heading to the response and "- x" added an item
to it. Every row is a card row now and the body is the card's quoted long text.
Its target is toolutil.FormatTarget, so a to-do GitLab sent no target object for
no longer renders "[](url)"; the project row reads the path GitLab sends rather
than the name it does not, and names the group for a to-do raised in one; the
pagination footer moved ahead of the guidance section; and the two confirmations
end their line, so the rule below them is a rule and not a setext heading.

The snippet card was a "| Field | Value |" table, which left "| Imported From |
|" on the page for every snippet GitLab marked imported without naming the
platform, and put the two clone URLs — values a reader copies verbatim — in
cells rather than in code spans. A page of project snippets is now given the
project actions: the personal ones it used to name answer 404 for every row on
such a page.

Event lines carry the push ref, the commit count and the newest commit title, and
the issue or merge request a comment hangs on. All four were dropped, so a push
event read as the bare word "pushed to" whichever branch it touched, and an event
with neither author nor timestamp ended "by , ".

The search headings count what the response can vouch for instead of printing an
inferred total as GitLab's own, a found merge request is marked as a draft, the
commit and milestone dates go through FormatTime, and an empty result is the one
sentence rather than a heading counting zero above it.

The license template detail passes the key, the nickname and the popular flag the
shared card has had rows for since it was written, and both template lists render
the popular flag through BoolEmoji rather than as "true" or "Yes".

Every Markdown expectation in these packages is now the whole rendered document.
A substring assertion is how a table that a list row had already closed stayed
green in the first place.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for integrations, hooks, feature flags, alerts and achievements

Ten packages move onto toolutil.Card and the shared list vocabulary:
achievements, alertmanagement, badges, clusteragents, customemoji,
errortracking, featureflags, ffuserlists, integrations and systemhooks.
Every one-object result is now a card written by Card and nothing else,
every collection a table opened by MarkdownTableHeader under
WriteListHeading, and every empty page the one sentence EmptyMessage
writes instead of a heading counting zero. The two local yesNo copies
are gone: a flag is BoolEmoji or Card.Bool, and a timestamp FormatTime
or Card.Time, which retires six //gitlab:allow-unescaped directives that
excused a raw instant.

The rendering defects the audit confirmed are closed with it.
achievements wrote its guidance section between the heading and the
table header in four formatters, which both swallowed the table — a
header directly under a paragraph line lazily continues it — and left
the section neither leading nor trailing, where ExtractHints finds
nothing and next_steps came back empty; the hints now close the
response. The three mutation formatters wrote GitLab's message as a
bare paragraph, where a value opening with '#' becomes a heading and
one carrying a fence swallows the table below it; it is a card row now.
clusteragents printed a freshly created agent token through a
hand-rolled fence and now shows it as the code span Card.Secret writes,
with the store-it-securely sentence supplied once by End; its hints name
canonical action IDs rather than 'get' and gitlab_get_cluster_agent_token,
neither of which the default dynamic surface answers. systemhooks gains
the alert-status column without which a hook GitLab had switched off
looked exactly like a healthy one, and its test result says GitLab sent
its own fixed sample payload and that the response does not report the
receiver's status. integrations names the scope its empty list is about,
and a read's hint no longer promises the stored configuration the get
output does not carry; integrationToItem publishes RFC 3339 rather than
Go's own time layout, which FormatTime cannot parse. featureflags names
the user list a gitlabUserList strategy targets, customemoji carries the
global ID the delete action takes, alertmanagement labels the metric
link with the caption whoever uploaded it typed and shows the file path,
and badges renders a preview as a preview instead of as a badge card
with an empty name and an offer to edit a badge that does not exist.

Every markdown test moves to its own markdown_test.go and asserts the
whole rendered document. A substring assertion is how the worst class
survived: a table a list row had already closed still matched
"| Status | merged |" and still passed.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for storage moves, imports, Geo, analytics, pages and credentials

Eleven packages move onto toolutil.Card and the shared list vocabulary:
projectstoragemoves, groupstoragemoves, snippetstoragemoves, bulkimports,
importservice, geo, groupanalytics, dorametrics, pages, groupcredentials and
groupsshcerts. Every one-object result is now a card, every collection a table
under a counted heading, and every hint names a canonical catalog action.

The rendering defects the audit confirmed in these files are closed with it.
groupcredentials wrote its hints between the heading and the table header of
both listings, which left the header lazily continuing the guidance list, so
neither table rendered and ExtractHints read nothing; the hints now close the
response and the pagination footer sits above them. projectstoragemoves kept a
hand copy of the storage-move renderer with a zone-less timestamp layout, no
empty branch and no entity link, and now delegates to the shared one like its
two siblings, which also gives the three the same next-step hints. The three
schedule-all confirmations interpolated their message into a bare paragraph,
where a value carrying a heading, a list item or an anchor tag reached the page
as markup; each is a card row now. Geo gains the selective-sync scope and the
replication details link it never showed, prints its flags as glyphs and its
timestamp in the display form, and renders the health check's own multi-line
output as a quote. Pages stops printing "Project #0" on every project-scoped
call, shows the verification code while a domain is unverified, and renders its
deployments as a nested collection. bulkimports renders a relation's import
counts only when the migration reported that relation, instead of three zeros
for one it never mentioned. importservice fills the rows its four cards
dropped: the relation type, the refs URL, the provider link, the full path, the
import source and the status name. DORA metrics render each date through the
display helper and each value without the four decimals that stamped false
precision on a deployment count.

Two formatters nothing could reach are deleted with their tests: pages'
delete and unpublish confirmations, which the destructive routes never call,
and importservice's gist formatter, whose action returns no output at all.

Every formatter test now asserts the whole rendered response rather than a
substring, which is the assertion shape that let a card open a table it never
filled and still pass.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for the instance surfaces

Move the eight instance-wide admin domains onto one Markdown vocabulary:
appearance, appstatistics, broadcastmessages, dbmigrations, features, health,
license and metadata. Every result about one GitLab object is now a card
written by toolutil.Card and nothing else, every list opens with
WriteListHeading and closes with WriteListFooter, and an empty list is
EmptyMessage's one sentence rather than a heading counting zero above it.

Six card-shaped results were two-column tables, which render as a table only
while nothing else has been written since the header: the appearance, the
statistics, the broadcast message, the feature flag, the license and the
metadata. Those are list items now, and the eleven //gitlab:allow-unescaped
directives the hand-written rows needed are gone, because every value reaches
the page through a write that escapes it. The twelve flags and timestamps
printed with %v or %s go through BoolEmoji and FormatTime.

The defects the audit confirmed in these files, and what each renders now:

- The appearance card rendered eight of the eighteen fields it publishes: the
  logos, the favicon, the PWA icon and description, the two message colors and
  all three guideline texts were fetched, published in the JSON and dropped
  from the Markdown. Every one is a row, the five pieces of Markdown an
  administrator typed are quoted bodies, and the description row is written
  only when GitLab sent one. The update result is a card of its own, headed by
  what happened, rather than the read card under a heading that said nothing
  had.
- The statistics card presented every figure as exact. It says what GitLab
  says about its own counts: above ten thousand they are approximations.
- The broadcast message card dropped the target access levels, so a message
  shown to maintainers alone read as one shown to everybody; they are named
  through AccessLevelDescription. The list showed the two instants as the
  RFC 3339 the handler stored rather than the display form every other table
  shows, and the card gained the font GitLab sends.
- The mark-migration result was one bare paragraph with the status
  interpolated into it, escaped by nothing: a status carrying a tag reached
  the page as markup and one carrying a line break added a heading and a list
  item of its own. It is two rows.
- The feature flag card rendered three fields of the definition GitLab ships;
  it renders all nine, the three tracking links included, as a nested object,
  and its state is escaped where the list already escaped it.
- The health card joined the revision to the version as "%s (revision: %s)",
  which printed an empty parenthesis whenever GitLab sent one and not the
  other; they are two rows. An error whose body is a proxy's HTML page is
  quoted rather than written into a line, and the five directives declaring
  the server's own constants safe are gone, since the card escapes both halves
  at the row that writes them.
- The license card rendered the licensee as "%s (%s) - %s", which read " () - "
  for a licensee GitLab sent nothing about; it is a nested object, as are the
  add-on seats, which the card published in its JSON and dropped from the
  Markdown entirely. Expiry is marked with the warning sign rather than the
  tick BoolEmoji gives a true, which on "Expired" reads as success. The two
  local time helpers duplicating toolutil's are gone, and an answer carrying no
  license is an error naming that, rather than a nil dereference in toItem or a
  card reading "License #0" with a blank plan, which reads as a valid license
  that is not there.
- The metadata card read "Version" twice in one flat list, GitLab's and KAS's;
  the agent server is a nested object, and it carries the Kubernetes proxy
  address the endpoint sends and this server publishes and the card dropped.

The tests pin whole responses rather than substrings, which is how the audit's
worst class survived: a table that a list row had already closed with a row
still asserted and still passing.

mergeCommit.message:
refactor(markdown): the card vocabulary for merge requests, CI/CD, repository content and packages (#717)

The second migration wave: the domains a model reaches through a
pipeline rather than through a person. Merge requests and their notes,
discussions, award emoji and resource events; the CI/CD family;
repository content; runners, environments, deployments and releases;
packages, the registry, dependencies, secure files and uploads.

The rule is the layer's rule, unchanged: one object is a card written by
`toolutil.Card`, a collection of objects sharing columns is a table, and
nothing else writes a card row by hand. A value the reader must copy
exactly goes in a code span, an access level goes through
`AccessLevelDescription`, an empty list through `EmptyMessage`, and a
time through the shared formatter rather than as GitLab sent it.

The served surface does not move, and the golden snapshots say so.

commit.message:
refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for the merge request family

Migrates mergerequests, mrapprovals, mrapprovalsettings, mrchanges,
mrcontextcommits, mrdiscussions, mrdraftnotes, mrnotes, mergetrains and
deploymentmergerequests onto toolutil.Card and the list vocabulary
(WriteListHeading, WriteListFooter, EmptyMessage, MdUserHandle/MdUserLink,
HintAction). Every card row now goes through Card and every table is a
collection of objects sharing columns.

mergetrains is the file the audit proved broken and it is rewritten first:
its card opened a "| Property | Value |" table and then wrote a list row
into it, which ended the table with no body and left every later
"| Status | merged |" on the page as literal pipes, while a test asserting
exactly that substring passed. Its whole output is asserted now, and the
runtime gate keeps it that way: the assertion that mergetrains is reported
becomes an assertion that it never is again, with iterationdata left as the
fixture that proves the gate still sees the class.

What the migration also fixes, beyond the shapes:

- the merge request card shows the four conditions it never showed: a locked
  discussion, a scheduled auto-merge, a rebase in progress and the merge
  error of the last attempt; and the pipeline row carries the status;
- every list heading counts what the response can vouch for instead of
  printing GitLab's zero above a table of rows;
- mrapprovalsettings no longer interpolates an empty scope into its heading
  and into gitlab_update__mr_approval_settings, a tool no surface registers:
  the registered formatter writes a scope-neutral heading and names both
  real update actions;
- approver and eligible names are escaped and linked to their profiles, and
  an approval timestamp is rendered by FormatTime rather than as GitLab sent
  it;
- mrchanges shows each patch as a fenced block under a byte budget, and says
  in the text which files GitLab truncated instead of listing their paths in
  a hint;
- mrdiscussions adopts the shared discussion renderer, so a thread reads the
  same whether it was listed or fetched, and a note shows its resolution
  state only when it is resolvable;
- the draft note row that read "MR ID" says it is the global id and not the
  IID, and its list truncates the note body on rune boundaries;
- deploymentmergerequests renders the merge request row the way every other
  merge request table does, the IID carrying the link;
- mrnotes lists internal notes as a column, matching issuenotes.

Every hint names a canonical action ID, which every surface resolves.
The tests assert whole output rather than a substring, which is how the
audit's worst class survived.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for notes, discussions, award emoji and resource events

commitdiscussions, epicnotes, awardemoji and resourceevents write every
one-object result through toolutil.Card and every collection through the list
vocabulary; epicdiscussions and snippetdiscussions/snippetnotes were already
thin delegators over the shared note and discussion renderers, and only what
they hand those renderers changed.

What the cards and lists render now:

- the commit discussion note card shows the diff position of a note anchored to
  a line, and shows a resolution state only for a note that can carry one, where
  it used to print "Resolved: false" for every note; the thread card renders its
  own flags as glyphs and one section per note. These two formatters are
  registered for the shared thread shapes every REST discussion domain aliases,
  and the registry keeps the first registration, so they are what a merge
  request, issue and snippet discussion render as too.
- the commit discussion list heading counts what the response vouches for rather
  than the length of the page.
- epic discussion notes carry the system flag into the shared view model, so a
  record GitLab wrote itself is marked rather than reading as a comment.
- the epic note card is the shared note card, so a note with no author shows no
  author row; the list renders the system flag as a glyph instead of "false",
  counts what the connection can vouch for, and drops the instruction to keep
  links from a table that has none.
- the award emoji card names what was awarded, in the heading and in a row of
  its own, and links the awarding user's profile; the list is a table with the
  heading count and the pagination footer the shared writers produce.
- the five resource event lists carry a heading count, a summary line and a
  pagination footer; the four event cards write rows instead of a two-column
  table, omit a deleted milestone or iteration rather than printing "(ID: 0)",
  and name the object an event hangs on as a type and a database ID rather than
  an "Issue #42" whose sigil reads as a per-project number.

Every empty list is one sentence through toolutil.EmptyMessage, with no heading
counting zero above it. The six //gitlab:allow-unescaped declarations in
resourceevents are gone with the raw interpolations they excused, and the six
table-row constants in resource_events.go with the tables they built.

The formatter tests assert whole documents rather than substrings.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for repository content

Migrates the branch, branch rule, commit, file, repository, submodule, tag
and wiki formatters onto toolutil.Card and the shared list vocabulary, and
closes the rendering defects the markdown audit confirmed in them (issue 697,
layer 2, work item L2-09).

Every one-object result is now a card written by Card and nothing else, and
every listing opens with WriteListHeading, closes with WriteListFooter or
WriteGraphQLPagination, and answers an empty page with EmptyMessage rather
than a heading counting zero. The static card gate drops from 117 findings
across these nine packages to none, and the runtime scan's structural,
absent-value and list-heading findings for them to none.

What changed for a reader beyond the shape:

- a branch card shows the three permission flags GitLab sends on every
  branch, so a reader can tell a branch they may push from one they may not,
  and its head commit is a nested object rather than a bare SHA;
- a protected branch names the roles its access levels stand for instead of
  printing the numbers, and says whether code owner approval is required;
- a commit card writes the author's address in parentheses rather than in
  angle brackets, which GFM turns into a mailto autolink, and carries the
  pipeline status it used to drop;
- a cherry-pick or revert run with dry_run, which GitLab answers with no
  commit at all, renders as "No Commit Created" instead of a commit card
  whose heading and every field were empty;
- a commit's timestamps go out in RFC 3339 rather than Go's default layout,
  which no display helper could parse;
- a file card carries the file's body, which it used to drop for every
  format that is neither an image nor binary;
- the repository tree marks a submodule as a commit object rather than a
  file, and the generated changelog notes and the blob body are fenced
  rather than written raw;
- the archive URL escapes its project path segment and its ref query value;
- a tag's list column is the commit it resolves to rather than the tag
  object, its message is quoted when it runs to several lines, and the tag
  object is shown only when it differs from the commit;
- a wiki page's body is quoted when it is Markdown and fenced with its own
  format otherwise, where the group wiki used to write it raw;
- the group wiki listing no longer opens with a guidance section above its
  own table header, which stopped the table rendering at all.

Every expectation in the tests of these packages is now the whole render:
the substring assertions they replaced are the shape that let a table which
had stopped rendering keep passing.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for the CI/CD domains

Migrate the eleven CI packages (pipelines, pipeline schedules, jobs, job token
scope, CI lint, project, group and instance variables, freeze periods, resource
groups and the CI/CD catalog) onto toolutil.Card and the shared list vocabulary
(WriteListHeading, WriteListFooter, WriteGraphQLPagination, EmptyMessage,
MdUserLink, HintAction), which takes the 71 hand-written card rows and the 2
flags printed with %v and %t in these files to zero, and deletes the eleven
//gitlab:allow-unescaped directives the values no longer need.

What a reader sees change:

- The pipeline, job, schedule, schedule variable, freeze period, resource
  group, catalog resource, lint result and job token settings cards are list
  items written by Card, so a row after a table, a quote or a fence is still a
  row, and every value is escaped at the write that renders it. The schedule
  and catalog cards were Field|Value tables, which stop being tables the moment
  anything else is written between their rows.
- A list heading counts what the response can vouch for: "Jobs (0)",
  "Pipelines (0)" and "Pipeline Schedules (0)" above a table of rows are gone,
  and the freeze period heading counts the total GitLab reports rather than the
  page. An empty list is one sentence rather than a heading counting zero above
  one.
- A pipeline and a job say when they are archived, in the heading and as a row:
  GitLab refuses a retry and a cancel on either, and nothing in the card said
  so. A job also says when it was erased and when its artifacts expire, and its
  hints name what its own state still allows rather than a retry that can only
  fail.
- The pipeline card carries the detailed status GitLab computes, but only when
  it says more than the status word already there.
- The wait results embed the pipeline and the job without their own heading,
  under one H3, so a response carries one H2 and one guidance section instead
  of a card nested in a card and a guidance section in the middle, where
  ExtractHints never looked.
- The job trace's truncation note says which end is missing: the log is cut at
  the first 100 KB and a failure is almost always at the end of it.
- The lint result lists the jobs GitLab expands the configuration into, which
  the output type has carried since the captured-response read and no rendering
  showed; its errors and warnings are table rows rather than list items, so a
  message beginning with '#' or '-' no longer opens a heading or a nested list.
- The job token settings name the restriction rather than the switch: inbound
  access "limited to the allowlist" rather than "enabled", which read as its
  own opposite.
- The catalog list shows the resource's full path instead of linking its
  webPath, which is relative to the instance root and resolved against whatever
  base the reading client had; its description is quoted prose, and the cell is
  cut on a rune boundary rather than a byte.
- The instance variable card names the environment scope GitLab sends, which
  the view model dropped.
- Hints name canonical action IDs through HintAction, so a hint never names a
  tool two of the three surfaces do not register: the schedule hints used to
  spell "the selected tool surface's pipeline-schedule update action".

The formatter tests assert whole output rather than substrings, which is how a
table row that a list row had already closed kept passing.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for runners, environments, deployments and releases

Migrates the eleven formatters of work item L2-11 onto toolutil.Card and the
list vocabulary: runners, runnercontrollers, runnercontrollerscopes,
environments, deployments, protectedenvs, groupprotectedenvs,
groupprotectedbranches, releases, releaselinks and groupreleases. A result
about one object is now a card of "- **Label**: value" rows, a collection is a
table under a heading the response can vouch for, and every listing ends with
one guidance section instead of opening with a hint bullet that swallowed the
table under it.

What the audit found in these files and what it renders now:

- the runner registration and authentication tokens were printed as bare
  Markdown; both are written as secrets in a code span, with the sentence
  saying the value cannot be read back, and a runner GitLab has just
  registered finally shows the token at all;
- the auth-token reset and the three registration-token resets shared one
  output type, so the registry served one formatter for the pair and every
  registration reset rendered under the authentication token's heading. The
  registration resets answer with RegTokenOutput, which carries the same
  fields under the same JSON keys, so the actions' schemas are unchanged;
- the runner, runner-job, environment, deployment, protected-environment and
  release list headings counted the total GitLab never sent, printing "(0)"
  above rows; they count what the response can vouch for;
- the protected-environment and protected-branch access tables printed a
  numeric 0 for the user and group a role rule is not about, and named
  neither the grantee nor whether a group rule reaches inherited members;
- a protected environment with approval rules of its own reported the single
  headline count GitLab sends beside them, which is not what gates a
  deployment;
- the environment card never said what was deployed to the environment, and
  offered "stop" for an environment already stopped;
- the deployment card never said it was blocked on approvals, and its hints
  named deployment.get and deployment.list, which are not catalog IDs: a
  deployment action is projected under the environment domain;
- the release milestones were joined and then escaped once, so a title
  carrying a pipe could split the row; each title is escaped on its own;
- an upcoming release rendered a future date as one already past;
- the release-link delete answered with the link card, offering an update and
  a delete of a link that had just gone. Delete answers with DeletedOutput,
  again the same fields under the same keys.

The runners detail card lists the projects and groups a runner serves rather
than counting them, and the runner-job and deployment rows link to the job and
the pipeline that ran them.

Every test that covered these formatters now pins the whole rendered document
rather than a substring, which is how a table a list row had already closed
kept passing its own assertions.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for packages, registry, dependencies, secure files and uploads

Move the ten package-and-artifact domains onto one Markdown vocabulary:
packages, containerregistry, protectedpackages, dependencies,
dependencyfirewall, modelregistry, terraformstates, securefiles, uploads and
attestations. Every result about one GitLab object is now a card written by
toolutil.Card and nothing else, every list opens with WriteListHeading and
closes with WriteListFooter, and an empty list is EmptyMessage's one sentence
rather than a heading counting zero above it.

Four card-shaped results were two-column tables, which render as a table only
while nothing else has been written since the header: the registry repository,
tag, protection rule and tag protection rule, the dependency export and the

  that section neither leading nor trailing and so unreadable by ExtractHints:
  the embed sits between the rows and the guidance, and the result is built by

  or Publish Failed, with "N of M files" counted from both lists, since
  TotalFiles is the number that succeeded.

  printing two empty labels, and the lock hint no longer points at
  gitlab_lock_terraform_state, which GitLab refuses on every call; it names the
  terraform CLI and gitlab_unlock_terraform_state for a stale lock.

  after the file kind, and the download hint pointing at no route is gone; its
  timestamps render in the display form.
- Package, attestation and protected-package patterns and digests are code
  spans, so an entity no longer renders as its own characters inside one.

The tests pin whole responses rather than substrings, which is how the audit's
worst class survived: a table that a list row had already closed with a row
still asserted and still passing.

commit.message:
refactor(markdown): migrate the token, key and credential cards onto toolutil.Card

accessrequests, accesstokens, applications, deploykeys, deploytokens,
impersonationtokens, keys, pipelinetriggers and runnercontrollertokens now
render a single object through toolutil.Card and a collection through the list
vocabulary. Every two-column "| Field | Value |" card and every hand-written
"- **Label**:" row is gone, so a row can no longer land inside a table another
write opened and render as literal pipes.

What the reader sees that they did not before: the access request's Locked
warning, its creator, and its access level as the role GitLab means with the
number beside it; the access token's granular scopes and last use; the SSH
key's expiry, last use and usage type, with its owner as a nested object
instead of a line that read "(ID: 0, @)" when GitLab sent none; the deploy-key
and pipeline-trigger lists' Expires column; and the impersonation list's
Revoked column. Every %t and %v flag is now a glyph, a negative condition
(revoked, expired, locked) is marked with the warning sign rather than the tick
BoolEmoji gives a true, and every timestamp goes through FormatTime, including
the four raw RFC 3339 strings the deploy-key and runner-controller lists used
to print.

Secrets go through Card.Secret, which puts the value in a backtick-sized code
span and adds the advice to store it exactly on the card that showed one, so a
get no longer tells its reader to keep a token it never printed. The deploy
token's secret was written bare until now. Every list heading counts what the
response can vouch for through WriteListHeading, every empty list is the one
EmptyMessage sentence rather than a heading counting zero above it, and the
preserve-links reminder is dropped from the tables that carry no link.

The access-request hints named an "approve" action that does not exist; they
now name accessrequests.approve_project and approve_group by canonical ID, as
do the keys and runner-controller hints that named individual tool names the
default surface does not register. accesstokens' local access-level table is
deleted for toolutil.AccessLevelDescription, and the impersonation-token
formatters move from impersonation_tokens.go into the package's markdown.go.

The 27 //gitlab:allow-unescaped directives the migration made stale are
deleted. The static card and bool/time rules report 0 sites in these nine
packages, down from 118; the runtime registry scan reports 16, down from 56.
Every markdown test in these packages now asserts the whole rendered document
rather than a substring.

refactor(users): write the user, email, key and attribute cards with toolutil.Card

Layer 2 of the Markdown card migration (issue 697) for internal/tools/users,
useremails, usergpgkeys, enterpriseusers, avatar and customattributes: every
result about one GitLab object is now written by toolutil.Card, and every list
by WriteListHeading, MarkdownTableHeader, MarkdownTableRow, WriteListFooter
and EmptyMessage. The static gate counted 71 hand-written card rows and 18
raw booleans or timestamps in these six packages and now counts none, and the
13 //gitlab:allow-unescaped directives they needed are gone with them.

What a reader sees change, beyond the shape:

- the avatar upload's narrow GitLab 19 answer gets a card of its own, instead
  of a user card printing an ID of zero and an empty email for it;
- the user card gains the bot, external and locked rows it never had, the
  lock marked with the warning sign rather than a tick, and writes the avatar
  as the link it is rather than as escaped text;
- the membership list is a real table under a heading counting the total
  GitLab reported, with the access level under the name GitLab gives it;
- an address GitLab has not confirmed says "awaiting confirmation" in the card
  and in the list, where the card wrote no row at all and the list a dash;
- the GPG key preview is the tail of the armored body rather than the header
  line and leading base64 that every key on an account shares;
- the avatar URL and the enterprise user handle are links, and the enterprise
  list's preserve-links hint now sits over a table that has one;
- a custom attribute's key and value are escaped card rows rather than two
  bullet-less lines a Markdown reader runs together into one paragraph;
- the deleted, success and two-factor flags are BoolEmoji rather than "true",
  "Yes" or a success glyph printed beside the word "false";
- the runner token and the personal access token are Card.Secret, which adds
  the store-securely sentence, and a granular token lists its granular scopes;
- every next step names a canonical action ID, which every surface accepts,
  rather than an individual tool name the default surface does not register.

UserMembershipOutput still carries no web_url, so the source name stays plain
text: making it a link would move the output schema, which this layer does not.

The tests for these formatters assert the whole rendered document rather than a
substring, which is the assertion shape that let a card open a table and write
list rows into it while every row the test named was found in the string.

refactor(access): render members, roles, SSO links and service accounts as cards

Layer 2 of the Markdown audit (issue 697) for the access domains: members,
groupmembers, invites, memberroles, groupsaml, groupscim, groupldap,
groupserviceaccounts and projectserviceaccounts. Every result about one
GitLab object now goes through toolutil.Card, and every list through the
list vocabulary: WriteListHeading, WriteListFooter, EmptyMessage,
MdUserLink and HintAction.

What that fixes, beyond the shape:

- Every access level is rendered with toolutil.AccessLevelDescription. The
  SAML link, the LDAP link, the invitation and the member role printed the
  bare integer, which is the one form a reader cannot act on.
- The invitation list counted len() in its heading under keyset pagination,
  where GitLab sends no total, and wrote each invitation as a run of
  Fprintf with the user name unescaped, so a name carrying a line break
  added a heading, a list item or a forged guidance section to the
  response. It is a table now, and its per-address messages are a nested
  collection sorted by key: Go randomizes map iteration, so the same answer
  used to render two different documents on two identical calls.
- The LDAP card was headed "LDAP Link: " with nothing after the colon
  whenever the link was filter-based, since such a link carries no common
  name; it is headed by the filter now. Its list wrote the guidance section
  above the table, where ExtractHints cannot read it and the bold count
  line lazily continued the last hint, and left the member role out.
- Both member cards were missing the membership state and the lock, and the
  project member list the membership and expiry columns. A lock is written
  with the warning sign rather than with the tick BoolEmoji gives a true.
- The group service account's token timestamps were formatted with a layout
  ending in a literal 'Z' whatever zone the instant was in, so a non-UTC
  time was published as a UTC one it is not; they go through
  toolutil.RFC3339Ptr, which converts before it formats.
- Both service-account cards now surface the granular flag and the granular
  scopes, which is where a granular token's real permissions live, and
  print the token through Card.Secret, which adds the store-it-now hint.
- The SCIM identity's external UID was fed to the cell escaper inside a code
  span, where "|" and "<" render literally; it is a code span
  helper now, in the card and in the table cell alike.
- Flags print as the emoji and timestamps through FormatTime everywhere,
  and the hints of every list are one trailing section rather than a
  paragraph in the middle of the document.
- groupserviceaccounts carried a second, unregistered copy of its four
  formatters at the end of group_service_accounts.go. Nothing called it and
  it had drifted from the registered one; it is removed rather than
  migrated twice.

Tests compare the whole rendered document rather than a substring, which is
how the audit's worst class survived: a table a list row had already closed
still asserted, and still passed.

Measured on these files: the static card and bool/time rules go from 102
sites (84 card rows, 18 raw flags or timestamps) to 0, with no stale
directive; the runtime scan goes from 64 findings to 9, all of them
hostile-value reports that the gate's own model raises against constructs
toolutil already contains (a link label whose ']' is backslash-escaped, and
a value inside a code span).

refactor(markdown): move the project family onto the card vocabulary

projects, projectmirrors, projectaliases, projectdiscovery,
projectimportexport, projectstatistics and namespaces render every
one-object result through toolutil.Card and every collection through the
list vocabulary, which closes the rendering defects the markdown audit
confirmed in them (issue 697, work item L2-04).

What a reader sees differently:

- A regex, a path, a clone address, a mirror URL, a host-key fingerprint,
  a correlation id and an alias name are code spans rather than cells fed
  to the cell escaper, so a push rule of `^(feat|fix):` reaches the model
  as the pattern GitLab enforces instead of `^(feat|fix):`.
- The project card names the two rows it left out: why a repository
  action answers with nothing (empty repository) and that the project is
  scheduled for deletion, read from whichever of the two keys GitLab
  sent.
- A push rule with no file-size ceiling says "unlimited" rather than "0",
  which said the opposite.
- The webhook card's name and URL are list rows rather than bullet-less
  label lines that rendered as one run-on paragraph, both escaped, and
  its URL-variable and custom-header keys go through the one writer of a
  redacted key table.
- Every flag is a glyph and every timestamp the display form, so nothing
  prints true, false or an RFC 3339 instant any more.
- A list heading counts what the response vouches for, an empty list is
  the one sentence rather than a heading counting zero above it, and a
  table with no link no longer tells the model to preserve links. The
  alias list writes its hints after the table, where they no longer leave
  it unrendered.
- A share result writes no row for an access role GitLab did not send,
  and its message, which interpolates the caller's own project_id, is
  escaped.
- Hints name canonical action IDs, the one form every surface accepts.

projects keeps no private copy of the access-level table or of the ISO
date helper: both route through toolutil. The tests compare whole
documents rather than substrings, and each package's whole-output
expectations pin the hostile-value containment.

refactor(groups): write the group, hook, push-rule and topic cards with toolutil.Card

Migrates groups, groupimportexport, grouprelationsexport, groupmarkdownuploads
and topics onto the one Markdown vocabulary: every result about a single object
is a card written by toolutil.Card, every list opens with WriteListHeading,
renders its table through MarkdownTableHeader/MarkdownTableRow and closes with
WriteListFooter, and an empty list is EmptyMessage's one sentence rather than a
heading counting zero above it. The static card rule reports 37 hand-written
rows and raw flags in these files before and none after; the runtime registry
gate reports 26 structural findings before and none after.

What a reader sees that they could not before:

- an archived group says so, on the card and as a column of both group lists;
- a hook's event list names all twenty-one flags HookOutput carries, where six
  of them (confidential issues and notes, emoji, resource access token,
  project, repository update) were dropped, so a hook subscribed to only those
  read as "none"; and the card renders the custom headers it carries, keys
  only, beside the URL variables it already showed;
- a push rule's file-size limit is always stated, "unlimited" when it is zero,
  where the row used to be left out; its patterns are code spans of the text a
  maintainer typed rather than entities they would copy back into the rule;
- the member table labels the user's account state as such and adds the
  Enterprise membership state as a column when GitLab sent one;
- the group projects table opens with a heading that counts what GitLab
  reported, and the relations-export status names the state (started, finished,
  failed) beside its number.

Three formatters were unreachable and are gone: the second upload-list and
relations-export renderers, registered for a value while the handler answers
with a pointer, and groupimportexport's dispatcher over `any`, which the
registry refuses because nothing looks a formatter up by an interface. The one
registration problem the shared baseline named is retired with it.

Also: the local access-level table in sharing.go is replaced by
toolutil.AccessLevelDescription, which names Planner, Minimal access and Admin
the copy did not; an upload's created_at is stored as RFC 3339 rather than
time.Time.String(), which no display helper can parse; and every
//gitlab:allow-unescaped directive the migration made stale is deleted.

The formatter tests move to each package's markdown_test.go and assert the
whole rendered response rather than substrings, which is how a table a list row
had already closed kept passing.

refactor(markdown): card and list vocabulary for issues, work items and epics

Migrate the nine issue, work item and epic packages onto toolutil.Card and the
shared list vocabulary (WriteListHeading, WritePagination,
WriteGraphQLPagination, EmptyMessage, MdUserHandle, HintAction), which takes
the 66 hand-written card rows and the 9 flags and dates printed without their
helper in these files to zero.

What a reader sees change:

- The issue, epic, work item, saved view, issue link, epic issue and
  statistics cards are list items written by Card, so a row after a table, a
  quote or a fence is still a row, and every value is escaped at the write
  that renders it. Descriptions become quoted prose under their label rather
  than a section heading, and a work item's raw description is quoted at last.
- Every issue, epic and work item list row carries the confidential marker and
  the state emoji, without which a reader could not tell a restricted object
  from an open one.
- The list headings count what the response can vouch for: "Issues (0)" above
  a table of rows is gone, and the related merge requests count the total the
  response reports rather than the page.
- The cursor line of the epic issue, work item, saved view and epic lists is
  written by WriteGraphQLPagination, after a blank line, so it no longer glues
  itself to the last table row; the saved view list writes one guidance
  section at the end instead of one above the heading and one below.
- Hints name canonical action IDs through HintAction, so a hint never names a
  tool two of the three surfaces do not register. The saved view hints named
  work_item_saved_view.update and .subscribe, which are no action's ID.
- The statistics card's heading no longer claims a scope: one output type
  answers the instance, group and project routes, so "All Issue Statistics"
  was the same word whichever asked.
- The epic issue table carries the global ID the assign and remove actions
  take, and links its reference.
- A work item's parent is a nested object rather than a reference with a
  sigil, since the query does not say whether it is an epic or an issue.

The global issue listing answers with its own type, ListAllOutput, defined
from ListOutput with the same fields and the same schema: the Markdown
registry is keyed by the Go type, so while both list actions shared one type
only one formatter could be registered and the global listing rendered under
the project listing's heading and hints.

The formatter tests assert whole output rather than substrings, which is how a
table row that a list row had already closed kept passing.

feat(audit): two gates for the card shape, reporting what the migration owes (#712)

A rule nothing checks is a convention, and the audit found 1921 call
sites that drifted from one. These are the two gates that make the card
shape mechanical, both **reporting rather than failing** in this layer:
the migration of the 197 formatter files is what turns them into
assertions, one package at a time, and a gate that failed today would
fail on work nobody has done yet. Work items L1-08 and L1-09 of issue
697.

**The static gate** is a `card` context in `cmd/audit_md_escaping`,
which already walks every Markdown sink in the tree. It reports a card
row written by hand: a constant line opening `- **Label**:`, a
bullet-less `**Label**:` line, a two-cell row whose first cell is a
constant label, and the `| Field | Value |` headers themselves, which is
what catches a row assembled across several writes. A second context
judges booleans and times: a `%t` in a sentence, a `*At` string printed
as GitLab sent it. Both are selectable by name and are never part of
`all`, so `make check-md-escaping` keeps its exit status while `make
audit-md-escaping` shows the work list. `Card.Markdown` and
`CardTable.Row` are registered as call-site sinks, so a raw value is
reported where the formatter passed it rather than inside `card.go`, and
`internal/toolutil` is now held to no unresolved value at all through
`-fail-unresolved-in`.

Making the classifier follow `append`, `make` and `new` surfaced six
real escaping bugs, which are fixed here: label names in
`groupepicboards`, milestone titles in `releases`, user and group names
at three sites in `mrapprovals`, and a truncated path inside a hint in
`mrchanges`.

**The runtime gate** reads what a client would render.
`internal/testutil` gains a GFM line model (fences, quotes, list items,
ATX headings, thematic breaks, tables with cells split on every
unescaped pipe) and a reflective fixture filler that fills every output
type with sentinels, URL-shaped and time-shaped values and four
pagination states. `TestMarkdownRegistry_*` drives all 586 cases (578
registered types plus the Markdown that lives outside the registry: the
dynamic surface's search, find and describe output, and the elicitation
results) and applies the table-boundary, geometry, block-separation,
hint-invariant, absent-value, list-heading and hostile-value rules.

What it reports today, which is the layer-2 work list measured rather
than estimated: **571 structural findings in 104 packages**, 51
absent-value findings in 25, 469 hostile-value findings in 63, and 12
registration problems. `mergetrains` and `iterationdata` are among them,
asserted by name, because those are the two files the audit proved write
a list row into an open table: a gate that did not report them would not
be a gate.

The envelope question moves to `cmd/audit_surface_quality`: every
registered formatter driven with a zero and a populated value must
return a non-nil result whose every content block carries annotations.
25 formatters return nil for a zero value and two blocks in `uploads`
carry no annotation.

One test was hiding the class rather than finding it: the coverage check
read only `<pkg>/markdown.go` and continued on a read error, which is
why `importservice`'s four formatters have been invisible. It now walks
every non-test file in the package and asserts per route.
