feat(audit): stage the card and bool-time rules, judge the Card writes, and hold toolutil to no unresolved value

The escaping audit gains the two static rules the markdown plan stages
before the migration, both selectable by name and neither part of "all", so
make check-md-escaping keeps its exit status while they report. The card
rule lists every one-object card row a formatter writes by hand instead of
through toolutil.Card: a constant "- **Label**:" or "- **Label**" line with
or without an emoji before the label, a bullet-less "**Label**:" line, a
two-cell table row whose first cell is a constant label, and the field-table
header in its four spellings, whether written as text, through a builder, a
print call, the TblFieldValue constant or MarkdownTableHeader. A row whose
label is a value, an author item, a collection row and a metrics table keyed
by a map key are not read as a card; the prompts and card.go itself are out
of scope. The bool-time rule asks a second question of every hole, what the
value is rather than where it lands: a flag printed by %t, a boolean under a
textual verb, strconv.FormatBool or a yes-or-no helper of the package's own,
and a time.Time under a textual verb, a Format with a layout of the
formatter's own, or a string field named like an instant printed as GitLab
sent it, through the escapers the first verdict sees through. The two
verdicts are independent, the raw one has its own //gitlab:allow-raw
directive, stale only in a run that judged it, and %t is collected so the
verdict can see it. Measured on the tree, 1396 card sites (1323 rows, 73
headers) and 247 raw flags or timestamps, which is the layer-2 work list
make audit-md-escaping now writes with -contexts all,card,bool-time.

Card.Markdown and CardTable.Row are call-site sinks, in the list item and
the cell they write, on the terms MarkdownTableRow already had: every other
Card method escapes what it is given, so a raw value passed to it reaches no
construct, while those two write the value as given and the finding belongs
to the formatter that composed it.

The gate holds internal/toolutil to no unresolved value, through
-fail-unresolved-in, a package-prefix form of -fail-unresolved that keeps
the rest of the tree reported: a blind spot in toolutil sits behind every
formatter that calls it. Getting there taught the classifier three shapes
it used to give up on. A slice allocated by make and built by append is
judged by what was appended, which resolved the two spread rows in the
shared list renderers and, with it, five real findings the unresolved
verdict had been hiding: label names, milestone titles, user names and
group names joined raw into a list item or a cell in groupepicboards,
releases and mrapprovals, each now escaped where it joins the sentence, and
the truncated file paths mrchanges listed raw in a hint. A caller that
leaves a variadic parameter empty passes nothing and is skipped rather than
read as a shape the audit cannot follow. And a verdict reached through a
caller names that caller by package, file and line, since the helper's own
line is not where the fix goes.

Three declarations answer what the classifier cannot follow to a literal:
the parameter name and the usage sentence a meta-tool description lists,
both compiled in from an ActionSpec, and the hint WriteHints writes. That
last one is declared rather than judged, with the measurement in the
reason: every hint a domain passes classifies safe, and the ten arguments
that do not are toolutil's own plumbing of those hints through an options
struct, a renderer constructor, a method receiver or a registered
formatter's output type. It fails the gate as stale the moment the
classifier follows those shapes. Card.End escapes the secret label it
writes into its hint, since the hint is a list item too.

The Markdown tables the earlier commits of this layer left with stale
padding are normalized, so go run ./cmd/format_md_tables/ --check passes.

Co-authored-by: Aysura Churpanova <mona@github.com>

test(tools): drive every Markdown formatter through a GFM line model and report what the client renders

The runtime structural gate the markdown plan calls the registry scan. Every
registered type, plus the renderers no registration reaches (the shared
iteration renderers two packages wrap, the elicitation outcomes, and the
dynamic surface's search, find and describe output), is driven through
MarkdownForResult with reflective fixtures and the text the client would
receive is read with a line model of the GFM block rules, which is the one
reader in the tree that applies a renderer's rules rather than a substring
check. The rules are the ones the audit proved the tree breaks: a table
header lazily continuing a hint bullet, a footer absorbed as a row, a card
row written inside a table with every row after it orphaned, a delimiter
that disagrees with its header, a rule turning a paragraph into a setext
heading, a footer continuing the last bullet, label lines with no bullet, a
guidance section ExtractHints cannot read or written twice, HintPreserveLinks
over a render with no link, a list heading counting the page rather than the
total or counting zero where GitLab sent no total, the sentinel instant
printed raw, a field GitLab omitted rendered as a glyph, and a hostile value
that changes the count of headings, items, rows, cells or hints or opens a
link to a destination the fixture never named.

Every rule reports and none gates in this layer: the findings are the
migration's work list, the exception map is the mechanism the layer that
turns a rule on will fill, and an entry naming no case fails. The one
assertion made now is the proof that the gate works: mergetrains and
iterationdata, the two files the audit proved broken, are among what it
reports. Measured on the tree, 571 structural findings in 104 packages, 51
absent-value findings in 25 packages and 469 hostile-value findings in 63
packages, over 586 cases and 1728 renders.

internal/testutil gains the two pieces the gate is built from. ScanGFM is
the line model: fences and quotes skipped as content, list items, ATX
headings, thematic breaks and indented continuations recognized by how the
line opens, a table as a pipe line followed by a delimiter row, cells split
on every pipe not preceded by a backslash, and a link only where a bracketed
label precedes the destination, since a bare closing half opens nothing.
FillFixture is the reflective filler: a sentinel of letters and digits per
string field, an address under gitlab.example for a URL-shaped one, the RFC
3339 sentinel for a time-shaped one, allocated pointers, two-element slices,
and the shared pagination shapes set by state, recognized by name and fields
rather than by package because the shared package imports this one from its
tests. OptionalFields and ZeroField are the differential's oracle and
mutation. The registry records the name of the function registered for each
type, so a finding names groupcredentials.FormatPATListMarkdown and not only
the type it renders.

The registration record is pinned to a baseline that may only shrink, and
it is longer than the audit knew: beside the runner token, the shared note
and discussion shapes are registered by every domain that renders them and
the first init to run wins for all, which is the same defect with more
surfaces behind it. The coverage test asks per route rather than per
package and reads every non-test file rather than markdown.go alone, which
is how a formatter kept in another file, or a route whose output type the
package never registered, stayed invisible; it holds one route today,
branch.unprotect, in a baseline that may only shrink.

cmd/audit_surface_quality ends its metadata view with a result-envelope
section, in the report and under the envelopes key of the JSON view: every
registered formatter driven with a zero and a populated fixture, counting
nil renders of a zero value apart from those of a populated value, and
listing every content block with no Annotations, every panic and the
registry's own record. It reports and does not gate: the dispatchers
annotate every text block on the way out, so the two bare blocks it lists,
both from the upload result, are a formatter building its own envelope
rather than a block the client sees bare.

The two tables the reflective filler's own tests walk asserted without a

fix(testutil): read an escaped bracket and a code span the way a renderer does

The two hostile-value rules of the runtime Markdown gate were each wrong at
their boundary, and both were wrong in the direction that costs a reader the
most: one reported 47 findings that were all false, the other hid findings it
existed to make.

X1's link scanner accepted a backslash inside a label without giving it any
meaning, so the escaped "]" that EscapeMdLinkLabel writes read as the end of
the label and every link this server builds around a hostile title was
reported as a link to the attacker's destination. CommonMark says the
opposite twice: an escaped character is a regular character with no Markdown
meaning, and brackets are allowed in link text when they are
backslash-escaped. A label character is now either a character that is not a
bracket, a backslash or a newline, or a backslash and whatever follows it,
which also keeps the real defect reported: the hand-written link that escapes
its title as a table cell still opens the value's own destination, and an
escaped backslash still leaves the bracket closing the label. The finding now
names the destination, the line and its text, since a count on its own could
not be triaged, and how many there are stays a count so that a formatter
whose destination half is a field the fixture does not recognize as an
address is not condemned for linking off-origin in both renders.

X2 was right and scanned the wrong text. It read the content lines, which
exclude fences and quotes but not inline code spans, so a value the migration
deliberately moved into a span was judged as though it were bare. ScanGFM now
carries a bare view beside Content: every line outside a fence with its code
spans elided, a row tokenized per cell first because GFM splits on unescaped
pipes before anything parses inline content. The blockquote question is
decided rather than inherited, and the decision is to judge those lines: the
quote is containment against structure and none at all against a tag, which a
client renders as a live anchor wherever it sits. Every offending line is
reported rather than the first.

Neither rule could be counted before the exemption join was fixed. Trailing
digits were stripped to drop a slice index, so SHA256 was looked up as SHA,
and a directive written on a local variable named no selector and mapped to
nothing. Both silently un-exempted a field its package had already declared
safe, against the join's own policy of erring toward exempting too much. A
path is now looked up under both spellings, and a local is resolved through
the values the package assigns it.

One real defect the rules found, and the one that proves X2 must survive:
gitlab_render_markdown concatenated GitLab-returned HTML into the page, so a
client that renders raw HTML showed a live anchor to whatever host the content
named and a client that suppresses it dropped the tag silently. Returning
rendered HTML is what the tool is for, so the answer is containment and not
escaping: the document goes inside a fence sized past the longest run of
backticks in it, under a line saying whose HTML it is.

Measured on the corpus: the link rule falls from 47 findings over 93 links to
none, and the raw-tag rule from 67 findings to 108 real ones, having dropped
five code spans and four cases the exemption join had un-exempted, gained
fourteen blockquote lines and forty-two lines the first-line break was hiding.

refactor(audit): name the verb a spread slice carries

The three sites that spell the spread verb are one fact about the sink model,
not three: a call that spreads a slice into a row names the slice and no
expression this pass can read, which is why the raw verdict declines it. The
constant says that once and the comment says why, so a reader who meets the
verb in a report finds the reason beside its definition.

commit.message:
refactor(toolutil): move the shared renderers onto Card and add the list vocabulary

The four card-shaped shared renderers now write through Card: the storage
move detail, the CI/CD variable detail, the note detail and the template
body. The discussion note view model is merged into NoteMarkdown, since a
thread note is a GitLab note like any other and the two renderers disagreed
on the heading, the author's spelling and the body's label, while the
discussion one carried no resolution state at all; FormatDiscussionNoteMarkdown
is gone and the renderer's FormatNote writes the same "Discussion Note #N"
card the merge request and commit discussion packages write by hand.

The list vocabulary the audit asked for is added: WriteListHeading counts
what the response vouches for (the total GitLab sent, or the count shown with
"more available" under keyset pagination, never a zero above rows),
WriteListFooter writes the pagination line after a blank line and leads with
HintPreserveLinks only over a table that carries a link, WriteGraphQLPagination
is the one way a cursor line is written, EmptyMessage is the one empty
sentence, MdUserHandle and MdUserLink spell an author, WriteHookSecretKeys
holds the two redacted key tables three packages copied, SeverityBadge with a
new EmojiOrange replaces the hand-typed code points in the two security
packages, HintAction names an action by its canonical ID, and mapSlice
replaces the seven identical mapping loops.

The findings this file owned are closed: the zone-less timestamps and the
"_Page N, M moves shown._" footer of the storage move list, its missing
empty branch and leading hint, the bold-label rows, the heading fallbacks
that printed a zero total, the note ID missing from a thread's note lines,
the author row written without the handle, the pipeline states the emoji
table lacked (scheduled, preparing, waiting_for_resource, canceling,
waiting_for_callback), the hand-written fence in the template body, and the
one-line description that left "<" and "|" raw. The pagination footer prints
what is known and nothing for a pagination GitLab never sent, and the summary
line names no total when there is none. FormatPagination and
MarkdownTableSeparator are unexported; the nine formatters that wrote the
footer by hand, six of them with no separating blank line, call
WritePagination. DateTimeFormat is deleted: its literal Z stamped whatever
wall clock a value carried, and the twenty-one converter sites write the wire
form through RFC3339Ptr. The dead AppendResourceLink, WriteEmpty,
FormatGraphQLDiscussionListMarkdown, FormatTemplateCollectionMarkdown,
NewTemplateMarkdown and TemplateMarkdowns are removed.

Every test that pinned a substring of a changed renderer now pins the whole
document, so a table row rendered as literal pipes cannot pass again.

Co-authored-by: Aysura Churpanova <mona@github.com>

refactor(toolutil): render labels and templates as cards, and name a note's author once

FormatLabelMarkdown and FormatTemplateDetailMarkdown write through Card. The
two per-caller switches are gone: LabelMarkdownOptions.EscapeDescription let
the project scope escape a description the group scope rendered raw, and
TemplateDetailMarkdown.PlainFields let the license family write bullet-less
label lines that rendered as one run-on paragraph. Each had exactly one
setter, and each made one entity answer the same question two ways; the
description is now the card's long text for every caller, escaped on its row
when it is one line and quoted under its label when it is not.

The label card renders its two flags as glyphs rather than "true" and
"false". The label list carries a Scope column, since a project's list mixes
its own labels with the ones it inherits from its groups, and writes its
heading, delimiter and footer through the shared list helpers instead of by
hand. FormatTemplateListMarkdown is merged into
FormatTemplateAttributeListMarkdown, which renders the two-column shape when
no attribute header is named, so the plain and the attributed template
families share one heading, one empty form and one footer. Both lists render
an empty result as the configured message alone.

NoteOutput and DiscussionThreadNoteOutput gain AuthorUsername and
ResolvedByUsername, and the five byte-identical noteAuthorUsername copies in
mrnotes, issuenotes, snippetnotes, mrdiscussions and commitdiscussions are
deleted; the epic note keeps its own, since its output type is not the shared
one. MarkdownNote fills the note view model with the flags and the resolution
state the thread note carries, which the view model used to leave out.

The count columns of the label list still print zero when the caller did not
ask GitLab for counts. Closing that needs the request flag carried on the
list output, which changes the served schema, so it is left for the labels
and grouplabels migration.

Every test that pinned a substring of a changed renderer now pins the whole
document.

fix(toolutil): dispatch a pointer to a registered type, and finish every result one way

MarkdownForResult dereferences a pointer before it looks a formatter up,
which is the question HasRegisteredMarkdownFormatter already answered: the
two disagreed, so a handler returning *ListOutput had a formatter the
coverage test could see and the runtime never called. That was the live
case in groupmarkdownuploads and the four importservice formatters. A typed
nil pointer renders nil rather than being dereferenced.

The registry now records what it used to swallow. A second registration for
one type is refused and the first is kept, since a registration that silently
replaced another is how runners' auth-token reset came to render the
registration-token heading; a string and a result formatter on one type are
recorded; and an interface-typed registration is refused, since it landed
under a key no concrete value looks up, which is what groupimportexport's
fourth registration did. MarkdownRegistrationProblems returns the record and
RegisteredMarkdownTypes returns the types themselves, the seam the runtime
structural gate drives. RegisterMarkdownAnnotated carries a content preset
the plain registration hard-coded away, and NormalizeResultMarkdown is the
one normalization every content block passes through, whichever constructor
built it.

The three dispatchers end in one tail, FinishToolResult: a nil result
becomes the JSON rendering, so a formatter returning "" no longer reaches
the client with no content block; every text block carries the annotation
the action's declared content kind resolves to, through
AnnotationsForContentKind, so the kind a spec declares and the annotation the
dispatcher serves cannot disagree; an image block carries ContentUser; the
next-step hints are set on the typed output through its own HintSetter; and
the canonical resource is embedded last, so its JSON carries the hints too.
The content kind travels on the route for that, beside the embedded resource
template.

The hints are set through the type and never spliced into its JSON: the
individual surface validates the structured output against the schema the
type declares, and a next_steps key on a type that declares none would fail
it. The individual dispatcher's WithHints call, with an `any` output, matched
neither of its two cases and dropped next_steps on every call; the meta
dispatcher's JSON splice added next_steps to any object. Both now set the
field where the type declares it and leave the Markdown as the only carrier
where it does not. ContentBoth, which nothing set, is deleted, and ContentUser
is what the image block of an upload carries.

fix(toolutil): carry every refusal in one annotated envelope, and render the safe-mode preview as a card

ErrorResultAnnotated is the one envelope a refusal travels in: IsError set,
the text normalized the way every success is, and an annotation on the block,
the refusal preset unless the caller names another. The five hand-built
mcp.CallToolResult literals that carried no annotation and skipped the
normalization now go through it: ErrorResult, NotFoundResult, the cancelled
confirmation, the rate-limit refusal and ErrorResultMarkdown, which is kept
as the one path a handler has to a rich error result.

The not-found result is a card: the heading names the resource, the
sentence names the identifier the caller typed with the bracket and the tag
escaped, and the domain hints follow. The DetailedError card is written with
Card: its four consecutive bullet-less label lines rendered as one run-on
paragraph and interpolated GitLab's message and details raw, while only the
request ID was escaped, at the wrong end, in the JSON field. Each field is
now a row, escaped where it renders, and the request ID is stored as GitLab
sent it.

Safe mode's preview is rendered as a card on every surface, through a
formatter registered for SafeModePreview, so the individual surface no
longer writes a JSON literal with no annotation while the dispatcher
surfaces wrote another. The card names the intercepted tool, echoes the
arguments in a JSON fence and ends with the operator's hint;
ParseSafeModePreview reads it back, and the tests on every surface, the e2e
suite included, read the preview through it rather than parsing the text as
JSON by hand.

An embedded resource block is annotated as the machine-facing detail it is,
and the canonical resource is documented as embedded after the hints, which
FinishToolResult does, so its JSON and the structured output are one
serialization. The two error-wrapping examples in the doc comments are
replaced by the compositions the tests pin.

feat(toolutil): add the one card writer and the value vocabulary it needs (#709)

Every tool result about one GitLab object is a card, and until now each
of the 741 formatters wrote one by hand in whichever of two vocabularies
it happened to pick. The audit of all of them (issue 697) settled on one
rule and one writer, and this is that writer plus the value vocabulary
it needs. Nothing migrates yet: every formatter renders exactly what it
rendered before, which is what makes the migration that follows
reviewable one package at a time.

`toolutil.Card` writes the H2 heading the formatter composes, one `-
**Label**: value` item per field, then long text as a quote indented
under its label, a nested object as a sub-list or an H3 section, a
nested collection as a table under an H3, and the hints last. It streams
into the caller's builder and separates itself from whatever else was
written there, so it composes with the seams formatters already have.
Every value is escaped at the write that renders it, by the helper that
value's shape needs, so `cmd/audit_md_escaping` judges `card.go` like
any other formatter rather than having to trust it.

The decisive evidence for the list over the table is in the tree rather
than in taste: `mergetrains/markdown.go` and `iterationdata/markdown.go`
each open a two-column table and then write `FmtMdID`, which ends the
table and turns every later `| Label | value |` into literal pipe text,
while `merge_trains_test.go` asserts `"| Status | merged |"` and passes.
Two parallel vocabularies whose names do not say which shape they belong
to is what allows that, so the answer is one vocabulary behind one
writer. The full argument, the method-by-method contract, the rendered
examples and the open items are in `docs/development/markdown-card.md`.

The prerequisites, which are work items L1-01 and L1-02 of the plan:

- `MdCodeSpan` and `MdCodeSpanCell` render a value the reader must copy
exactly, with a fence sized past the value's own backtick run and no
entity encoding, and the escaping gate knows both.
- `EscapeMdTableCell` and `EscapeMdHeading` entity-encode the opening
bracket, so a GitLab title typed as a complete Markdown link renders as
text rather than as a link the model is told to preserve. A link is
built by `MdTitleLink` from its raw halves and never escaped afterwards:
`FormatTarget` escaped its title twice, and three formatters escaped a
finished link, all fixed here because the new escaping made them render
`[`.
- `EscapeMdLinkDestination` percent-encodes the pipe and the line
endings, so a URL cannot split or end the cell its link sits in.
- `RFC3339`, `RFC3339Ptr` and `FormatTimeValue` name the wire form and
the display form apart, which is what produced a card printing RFC 3339
into a table.
- `WriteHints` trims trailing newlines and writes a blank line before
its rule, so a preceding line can no longer be absorbed into a setext
heading. That closes the class at eleven call sites by construction
instead of one at a time.

The tests hold hostile values as a property rather than as examples: a
pipe, a CRLF, a leading `#`, a backtick run,
`x](http://attacker.invalid/)`, a complete link, an HTML anchor, a
forged guidance section and a forged table each change no structure, and
every method carries whole-output expectations beside that. Six
invariants are stated in the design document and pinned by tests, which
is what the two gates of the next layers will enforce mechanically.

fix(tools): stop rendering credentials in tool Markdown (#708)

A read of all 741 registered Markdown formatters (issue 697) found seven
places where a credential reaches the model's transcript. Each was
confirmed by two independent verifiers reading the formatter and the
value it renders, so none of them is theoretical, and none of them waits
for the card rule that audit settled on.

- `pipelinetriggers` printed the whole trigger token on every get and
once per row on every list. GitLab returns it on those endpoints, so
rendering it was our choice: the create card, which mints the token,
still prints it in full inside a code span, and every other card and row
prints the `glptt-` prefix and four characters, with a hint naming where
the full value is. A token too short to mask reads `[redacted]`.
- `runners` wrote the authentication and registration tokens as bare
Markdown, and an empty `**Token**:` line when there was none.
`runnercontrollertokens` did the same and wrote "Store the token value
securely" on a get carrying no token. `users` printed a runner token
with no code span and no guard. All four now follow the form
`accesstokens` already used: the value inside backticks, written only
when it is there.
- `instancevariables` rendered the value of a variable the instance
marks Hidden. The shared renderer already had both halves of the guard,
so the card adopts it: `!Masked && !Hidden`, with the Hidden flag shown
as its own row.
- `repositorysubmodules` resolved
`https://user:password@host/group/project.git` by taking the SCP branch
on the `@` and the `:`, which published the password in the rendered
path and in the `url` field of the structured output. The SCP branch is
now taken only for a remote with no scheme; anything else goes through
`net/url` with the userinfo dropped, and the published field is redacted
the same way.
- `prompts`' webhook audit masked a URL by printing its first thirty
characters, which is the userinfo and the front of a secret path. It now
renders the origin alone.

The redaction both ends needed is one file,
`internal/toolutil/url_redact.go`: `RedactURL` drops userinfo, query and
fragment and keeps the path, which is what a health check wants and what
the unexported helper in `internal/tools/health` already did;
`RedactURLToOrigin` drops the path as well, for a destination whose path
is the secret. They are separate functions on purpose rather than one
rule forced on both callers.

Each fix carries a test that fails on the old code by asserting the
secret's absence and the redacted form's presence, not merely that the
output changed.

Two things worth stating because they bound what this buys. The trigger
token is still in the structured JSON on get and list, since removing it
would break the 1:1 mapping with GitLab's own response; the Markdown is
the editorial surface and the hints now say where the full value is. And
an SCP remote keeps its `git@`, which is the ssh account rather than a
secret: only a userinfo carrying a password is stripped.

commit.message:
fix(tools): stop rendering credentials in tool Markdown

Seven formatters wrote a live credential into the Markdown this server puts in
front of a model. Each is withheld, masked or code-spanned now, and each has a
test that fails on the old rendering.

- Pipeline triggers: the get and the list cards printed the whole trigger
  token, a list once per row. They print GitLab's "glptt-" marker plus four
  characters now, and the full token stays on the create card alone, which is
  the call that mints it. The structured output is untouched, so the 1:1
  mapping with GitLab's own response holds.
- Runners: the authentication and registration token cards wrote the token as
  bare Markdown and announced an empty Token when there was none. Both write it
  inside a code span now, and only when it is there.
- Runner controller tokens: the same code span, and the advice to store the
  token securely is written only on a card that carries one, since a get
  answers with the same type and no token.
- Users: the created runner's token gets the same code span and guard.
- Instance CI/CD variables: a variable GitLab marks hidden had its value
  printed, because the card asked only whether it was masked. The card
  delegates to the shared renderer now, which has held both halves all along
  and reports the flag as well.
- Repository submodules: a remote is resolved by its scheme rather than by the
  presence of an "@" and a ":", so "https://user:password@host/group/project"
  no longer resolves to the password as the project name, and the url field the
  tool publishes carries no credentials either.
- Project audit prompt: the webhook table showed the first thirty characters of
  each hook URL, which is enough to spell out a userinfo and the front of a
  secret path. It shows the origin alone.

The URL rule the health tool already applied becomes toolutil.RedactURL, with
toolutil.RedactURLToOrigin beside it for a destination whose path is itself the
secret. Both are used rather than copied.
